page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AES, and SHA-ni. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also highly competitive, ranking in the top 10%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is strong, though read bandwidth and multi-core CPU performance fall into the average range. Conversely, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and static web serving throughput show weaker relative performance.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, this server offers a resource-dense profile that is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight caching layers, while being less optimal for highly parallelized database operations or high-throughput web serving.
